chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washsha, from Aasim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza, from Yahya ibn Uqayl, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'I fear for you only two things: following personal desires and lengthening of hope. As for following personal desires, it turns one away from the truth; and as for lengthening of hope, it causes one to forget the Hereafter.'
ai.seo_question: What are the two things Imam Ali fears most for his followers?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) diagnoses the root causes of spiritual deviation as *ittiba' al-hawa* (following whims) and *tawall al-amal* (prolonged hope in worldly life). This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on self-discipline, where unchecked desires obscure divine truth, while excessive attachment to temporal life dulls the consciousness of death and the Hereafter.
